It Must Have Been the Roses

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Scarlet Begonias** (3 reviews): The transition into Fire On The Mountain is particularly noteworthy in this recording; Reviewer considers this the best performance of the transition into Fire On The Mountain [12][13][19]
- **Estimated Prophet** (2 reviews): Reviewer cites the transition into Eyes Of The World and Wharf Rat as favorites; Post-jam into Eyes Of The World is slinky, reflecting a disturbed Garcia [13][19]
- **Cassidy** (1 review): Reviewer describes the performance as smooth, alongside a tight first set [15]
- **Fire on the Mountain** (1 review): Reviewer highlights a great performance of this song and a nice Cassidy [16]
- **Alabama Getaway** (1 review): Opening with this song signaled the band was going to rock the audience [18]
- **Loser** (1 review): Reviewer describes the performance of this song as sweet [21]

## The recordings

- **gd1981-02-27.139732.fob.beyer.m160.streeter.miller.clugston.flac2496** (recommended): audience recording; 21 songs; 159 min [1]
- **gd1981-02-27.176326.sbd.phase.repaired.mcgee.chief.miller.clugston.flac1644**: soundboard; 18 songs; 156 min [5]
- **gd81-02-27.glassberg.steinthal-cohen-vernon.20344.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 19 songs; 159 min; rated 4.33/5 by 6 [6]. Said about its sound: Reviewer is surprised by the high quality of this audience recording [16]
- **gd1981-02-27.176367.nak700.glassberg.menke.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 18 songs; 163 min [7]
- **gd81-02-27.sbd.lutch.4598.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 17 songs; 147 min; rated 4.27/5 by 41 [11]. Said about its sound: Transfer azimuth adjustment eliminated analog hiss, even when listening through headphones; Vocals and background vocals are crystal clear, with well-balanced instrumentation [12][21]

## Around the show

- Tapers in the audience asked each other if they felt anything between first set songs [14]
- Tapers stopped talking by the end of the Scarlet Begonias to Fire On The Mountain transition [14]
- Band members reportedly enjoyed playing in Chicago, contributing to the show's energy [18]
- Show described as fantastic, hot, sweaty, intimate, jam packed, and rocking [26]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1981-02-27.139732.fob.beyer.m160.streeter.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Frank Streeter; transferred by Charlie Miller and Scott Clugston; source: Source Info: Frank Streeter's Master FOB Audience Cassette; Beyer M160 (patched out of Rip Thompkins)> Sony TC-D5M (Maxell MX90); Transfer Info: Cassette… [1]. Also: Barry Glassberg's Nakamichi 700 source supplied crowd and tuning patches [1]
- **gd1981-02-27.176326.sbd.phase.repaired.mcgee.chief.miller.clugston.flac1644**: taped by David McGee and Chief; transferred by Vocal Phase Repair by Charlie Miller December 2025 Mastered by Scott Clugston January 2026; source: Master Soundboard Cassette > ? > DAT (16/44.1k) [5]. Also: Barry Glassberg and Bob Menke's Nakamichi 700 source supplied specific patches [5]
- **gd81-02-27.glassberg.steinthal-cohen-vernon.20344.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Barry Glassberg; transferred by John Steinthal; source: Audience Recording [6]
- **gd1981-02-27.176367.nak700.glassberg.menke.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Barry Glassberg; transferred by Bob Menke, Charlie Miller, Scott Clugston; source: Barry Glassberg's Master Audience Cassettes: Nakamichi 700 mics > Sony TCD5M (Maxell UDXL II) [7]. Also: Joe B. Jones assisted with pitch correction for this recording [7]
- **gd81-02-27.sbd.lutch.4598.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Dick Latvala; source: Soundoard [11]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Gapers Block: [1981 Grateful Dead show at Uptown Theater featured on Archive.org](http://gapersblock.com/transmission/2012/05/23/1981_grateful_dead_show_at_uptown_theater_featured_on_archiveorg/) [28]
